notes.1a: Most candidates were able to distinguish between capital and accumulated fund.
notes.1b: This part was well answered with a significant number of candidates scoring full marks. Although the question asked for the restaurant profit to be clearly identified some candidates ignored this and listed the restaurant income and expenses separately within the income and expenditure account thus not providing a profit or loss.
notes.1c: Few candidates were able to provide an appropriate explanation on why a club may capitalise donations.
notes.1d: This was not answered well with many candidates recommending short term sources of finance.
notes.2a: This topic was new to the specification and had not been examined before and was very well answered by most candidates. The most common error was the omission of the closing inventory.
notes.2b: This account was well prepared. Some candidates did not show the balance due from Bashmir even though the question clearly asked for this.
notes.2c: Most candidates were aware that the balance was a current asset.
notes.2d: Most candidates were able to make these calculations correctly.
notes.2e: The evaluation was generally well made. Most candidates decided that as Ahmed had made a profit he should have entered the joint venture and were rewarded accordingly.
notes.3a: Many candidates were unable to calculate the cost of the machinery and consequently could not determine the provision for depreciation.
notes.3b: Candidates answered this part reasonably well. Some candidates did omit the net book value section.
notes.3d: This part was not well answered. Few candidates considered the depreciation on the new machinery. Most evaluation did not consider the efficiency of the old machinery and its impact on revenue and costs in the future. �PAGE�20 9706 Accounting June 2016 �PAGE�21
notes.4a: Most candidates were able to calculate the ratios correctly but a significant number did not give their answers to two decimal places as was required by the question.
notes.4b: Most candidates provided acceptable comparisons of performance. Answers were generally well organised and well presented.
notes.4c: Most candidates were able to follow their comparisons through to advise Alfredo appropriately. The evaluation of the price earnings ratio often indicated a lack of understanding.
notes.5a: Most candidates calculated the overhead absorption rate correctly. Few candidates calculated the rate separately for the two products.
notes.5b: This was well answered by most candidates. Nearly all candidates calculated the selling price correctly.
notes.5c: This was also well answered and the activity based calculation was invariably performed correctly. However, many candidates did not state whether the change in selling price of each product was an increase or a decrease..
notes.5d: Few candidates were able to explain three differences and many merely stated that activity based costing is more accurate.
notes.5e: Many candidates repeated their answers from part (d) and very few attempted to relate their advice to the two products as was required.
notes.6a: Many candidates described both methods rather than distinguishing between them as was required.
notes.6b: The net cash flow calculations were made to a high standard. Some candidates omitted the maintenance check-up cost.
notes.6c: Nearly all candidates calculated the payback period correctly.
notes.6d: Nearly all candidates were able to calculate the net present value correctly.
notes.6e: The analysis was well answered with candidates generally commenting on the increased production levels and its implications. Most candidates gave an appropriate recommendation and justification.
notes.general_comments:
Overall performance was very good with some very good scripts.
Questions 2 and 6 were answered better than questions 1, 3 and 5.
